name: Dummy Deck
description: Sandbox for testing new technical phrases before migration.

cards.sideA: El audio se sobrepone al tener los 2 micrófonos abiertos.

sideB.text: The audio overlaps when both microphones are open.
The audio overlaps when you have both mics on.
Having both microphones open causes the audio to overlap.
The audio overlaps when 2 microphones are open.
The audio gets overlapped when both microphones are open.

cards.note: ~The audio gets overlapped having both microphones open~ sounds unnatural because the clause [having both microphones open] needs a connector. It is better to say [when having] or use a subordinate clause like [when both microphones are open].

cards.sideA: Toca cada tarjeta de marca aquí.

sideB.text: Tap each brand tile here.
Tap on each brand tile here.
Tap each brand card here.

cards.note:
In UI design, a [tile] is usually a flat, clickable square or rectangle that navigates to a new section or launches an app, whereas a [card] often contains more complex, heterogeneous information (text, images, buttons) grouped together.

~Touch each brand tile here~ is understandable, but for digital interfaces and screens, the correct verb is [tap]. [Touch] is generally used for physical contact rather than interacting with a UI element.

cards.sideA: Los bloques de marca mejoraron las ventas.

sideB.text: Brand tiles improved sales.
Brand tiles boosted sales.
The brand tiles improved sales performance.
Brand tiles improved the sales.

cards.sideA: Cuando A es diferente de B, podemos acceder.

sideB.text: When A is different from B, we can access it.
When A differs from B, we can gain access.
We can access it when A is different from B.
When A is different to B, we can access it.

cards.note: ~When A is different from B, we can access~ is missing an object. The verb [access] is transitive in English and requires a direct object (e.g., [access it], [gain access]).

cards.sideA: Las devoluciones usan bandejas.

sideB.text: Returns use flats.
Returns are processed using flats.
Flats are used for returns.
Returns use trays.

cards.note: In logistics and mail sorting, a [flat] refers to a large envelope, magazine, or a flat sorting tray. A [tray] is a shallow container used to hold, sort, or carry items.

cards.sideA: Solo espero que no se corte la luz.

sideB.text: I just hope the power doesn't go out.
I just hope we don't lose power.
I only hope the electricity doesn't go out.
I just hope the power doesn't cut off.
I just hope the power doesn't cut out.
I just hope the power doesn't go off.

cards.sideA: Quiero la mitad del pastel.

sideB.text: I want half of the cake.
I want half the cake.
I would like half of the cake.
I want a half of the cake.

cards.note:
**[er:229]**

~I want the half of the cake.~ is not valid because [half] does not take 'the' in front of it in this structure. The natural forms are [half the cake] and [half of the cake], and with an article it becomes [a half].

[Half] functions as a predeterminer, meaning it comes before the article, not after it. This behaves similarly to 'all' or 'both' (e.g., you say 'all the cake', never 'the all cake').

cards.sideA: Quiero la cuarta parte del pastel.

sideB.text: I want a quarter of the cake.
I want one fourth of the cake.
I would like a quarter of the cake.
I want a fourth of the cake.

cards.note:
**[er:229]**

~I want the quarter of the cake.~ and ~I want quarter of the cake.~ are not valid because 'quarter' is a singular countable noun and requires the indefinite article [a]. The correct expression is [a quarter of].

cards.sideA: Desde dónde estamos obteniendo la información está muy lento.

sideB.text: Where we are getting the information from is very slow.
The place we are getting the information from is very slow.
The source we are pulling the information from is very slow.

cards.note:
**[er:230]**

~From we are getting the information is very slow.~ is not valid because a clause cannot begin with the bare preposition in this pattern. The clause starts with the wh-word and [from] stays at the end: [where we are getting the information from].

~Where we are getting the information is very slow.~ is not valid because the verb phrase 'get information' requires a source, so the preposition [from] must be included at the end of the clause.

cards.sideA: No construyas las vistas que quedan aún.

sideB.text: Don't build the remaining views yet.
Do not build the views that are still left.
Don't build the views that are left yet.

cards.sideA: Le mantendremos informado sobre nuestro progreso.

sideB.text: We'll keep you posted on our progress.
We will keep you updated on our progress.
We'll keep you posted with our progress.
We'll keep you informed about our progress.

cards.note:
**[er:231]**

~We'll keep you inform about our progress.~ is not valid because [inform] is the base verb and cannot describe the state of a person. After [keep + object] the word must be an adjective or a participle, so the correct form is [keep you informed], the same pattern as [keep you posted] and [keep you updated].

cards.sideA: ETA significa Tiempo Estimado de Llegada.

sideB.text: ETA stands for Estimated Time of Arrival.
ETA means Estimated Time of Arrival.
The acronym ETA refers to the Estimated Time of Arrival.

cards.sideA: ¿Cuál sería el tiempo estimado de llegada de los arreglos?

sideB.text: What is the ETA for the fixes?
What is the Estimated Time of Arrival for the fixes?
What is the estimated completion time for the fixes?

cards.sideA: Nombres largos no se muestran correctamente.

sideB.text: Long names are not displayed correctly.
Long names do not show up properly.
Long names are not rendering correctly.

cards.note: ~Long names are not showed correctly~ is not standard because the preferred past participle of [show] is [shown]. Additionally, ~Long names are not showed up correctly~ is invalid because the phrasal verb [show up] means 'to appear' and is not used in the passive voice. Instead, use the active form [Long names do not show up].

cards.sideA: Nombres largos se ven cortados, no completos.

sideB.text: Long names look cut off, not complete.
Long names appear truncated instead of full.
Long names are getting cut off rather than showing in full.
Long names are displayed cut off, not complete.

cards.sideA: compileSdkVersion indica la versión de Android con la que se compila la app.

sideB.text: compileSdkVersion sets the Android version used to compile the app.
compileSdkVersion indicates which Android version the app is compiled with.
compileSdkVersion defines the Android version that compiles the app.

cards.note: ~...sets the Android version is compiled the app~ lacks the proper sentence structure. It needs a relative clause and a preposition at the end, such as [the Android version the app is compiled with].

cards.sideA: targetSdkVersion define la versión de Android para la que está optimizada la app.

sideB.text: targetSdkVersion defines the Android version the app is optimized for.
targetSdkVersion sets the Android version the app targets.
targetSdkVersion specifies which Android version the app is optimized for.

cards.sideA: Gradle automatiza la construcción y empaquetado del archivo binario.

sideB.text: Gradle automates building and packaging the binary file.
Gradle automates the build and packaging of the binary file.
Gradle handles building and packaging the binary automatically.

cards.note: ~Gradle automates the contruction~ is not natural in a tech context. The industry standard term for compiling software is [building] or [the build], rather than construction.

cards.sideA: Gradle gestiona las dependencias y las tareas de compilación.

sideB.text: Gradle manages dependencies and compilation tasks.
Gradle handles dependencies and build tasks.
Gradle takes care of dependencies and compilation tasks.

cards.sideA: Kotlin se usa para escribir la lógica principal de la app.

sideB.text: Kotlin is used to write the core logic of the app.
Kotlin is used for writing the main logic of the app.
We use Kotlin to write the core logic of the app.

cards.sideA: Kotlin compila el código fuente en instrucciones ejecutables para Android.

sideB.text: Kotlin compiles the source code into executable instructions for Android.
Kotlin turns the source code into executable instructions for Android.
Kotlin compiles the source code into instructions Android can execute.

cards.sideA: Android Gradle Plugin es la extensión de compilación que adapta Gradle para compilar y empaquetar aplicaciones Android.

sideB.text: The Android Gradle Plugin is the build extension that adapts Gradle to compile and package Android apps.
AGP is the build extension that lets Gradle compile and package Android applications.
The Android Gradle Plugin extends Gradle so it can compile and package Android apps.

cards.sideA: Android Gradle Plugin es la herramienta oficial que procesa los recursos de Android para generar el binario final.

sideB.text: The Android Gradle Plugin is the official tool that processes Android resources to generate the final binary.
AGP is the official tool that processes Android resources to produce the final binary.
The Android Gradle Plugin is the official tool that handles Android resources to build the final binary.

cards.sideA: Usando 0.1 de opacidad significa que el color es casi totalmente transparente.

sideB.text: Using 0.1 opacity means the color is almost completely transparent.
An opacity of 0.1 makes the color nearly fully transparent.
Setting the opacity to 0.1 leaves the color almost invisible.

cards.note: ~Using 0.1 of opacity~ is unnatural because in English we omit the preposition and say [0.1 opacity], or use the structure [an opacity of 0.1].

cards.sideA: Usando 0.9 de opacidad significa que el color es casi totalmente sólido.

sideB.text: Using 0.9 opacity means the color is almost completely solid.
An opacity of 0.9 makes the color nearly fully solid.
Setting the opacity to 0.9 leaves the color almost completely opaque.

cards.sideA: La opacidad mide el nivel de transparencia de un elemento.

sideB.text: Opacity measures the transparency level of an element.
Opacity indicates how transparent an element is.
Opacity is the measure of how see through an element is.

cards.sideA: Con opacidad alta el elemento es más sólido y opaco.

sideB.text: High opacity makes the element more solid and opaque.
With high opacity the element looks more solid and opaque.
The higher the opacity, the more solid and opaque the element becomes.

cards.sideA: Con opacidad baja el elemento es más transparente y se ve menos.

sideB.text: Low opacity makes the element more transparent and less visible.
With low opacity the element looks more transparent and harder to see.
The lower the opacity, the more transparent and less visible the element becomes.

cards.sideA: Arrastra ese archivo y suéltalo allá.

sideB.text: Drag that file and drop it over there.
Drag and drop that file over there.
Grab that file and drop it right there.

cards.sideA: El contenedor envuelve la lista y elimina los huecos.

sideB.text: The container wraps the list and removes the gaps.
The container wraps around the list and gets rid of the gaps.
The container wraps the list, removing the gaps.

cards.sideA: Este componente envuelve la imagen para que no queden huecos.

sideB.text: This component wraps the image so there are no gaps.
This component wraps around the image to avoid any gaps.
This component wraps the image so that no gaps are left.
This component wraps the image to not have gaps.

cards.note: [Gap] means an empty space or opening between two objects or elements.

cards.sideA: Si el menú envuelve el texto, el hueco desaparece.

sideB.text: If the menu wraps the text, the gap disappears.
When the menu wraps the text, the gap goes away.
Wrapping the text with the menu makes the gap disappear.

cards.sideA: Espero que la solicitud devuelva una respuesta HTTP 200.

sideB.text: I hope the request returns an HTTP 200 response.
I expect the request to return an HTTP 200 response.
Hopefully the request comes back with an HTTP 200.

cards.sideA: Vamos a probar primero el happy path de esta función.

sideB.text: Let's test the happy path of this feature first.
First, we are going to test the happy path of this feature.
Let's start by testing the happy path for this feature.

cards.sideA: Parece que solo probaron los happy paths.

sideB.text: It seems like they only tested the happy paths.
It looks like they only tested the happy paths.
Apparently they only tested the happy paths.
It seems they only tested the happy paths.

cards.sideA: El happy path es el camino directo hacia el resultado sin complicaciones.

sideB.text: The happy path is the direct path to the result without complications.
The happy path is the straightforward route to the result with no complications.
The happy path is the direct route to the expected result without any issues.

cards.sideA: ¿No debería ser todo al mismo tiempo, como en la versión Mobile?

sideB.text: Shouldn't it all be at the same time, like in the Mobile version?
Shouldn't everything happen at once, like in the Mobile version?
Shouldn't it all be at the same time, the way it is in the Mobile version?
